# [Project name]

**Status: authoring template; no project implementation is implied.**

## Problem Statement

[User, task, inputs and the cost of failure.]

## Objectives

[Measurable functional and quality goals.]

## Architecture

[Component boundaries, interfaces and data contracts.]

## System Flow

[Input → processing → output; describe errors and backpressure if streaming.]

## Dataset

[Official name/source/license, download and preparation commands, expected layout, split policy and leakage checks. Include a small synthetic smoke option.]

## Installation

[Python and libraries, OS, CPU/GPU needs and exact setup commands.]

## Folder Structure

[Describe code, configurations, tests and generated artifacts.]

## Configuration

[Parameter defaults, units, ranges and environment variables.]

## Training

[For ML: seed, model, weights, versions, hardware, epochs, batch size, learning rate, splits and checkpoints. For non-ML: explicitly explain why training is not applicable.]

## Evaluation

[Protocol, held-out data, metrics, thresholds, uncertainties and failure cases.]

## Inference

[Exact command, request schema or function call with a small example.]

## Results

[Actual measured outputs with context, or clearly marked expected output if unexecuted. Never invent numeric results.]

## Screenshots

[Generated from the running implementation; include captions and input provenance.]

## Limitations

[Scope, unsupported inputs, assumptions and untested settings.]

## Future Improvements

[Concrete next experiments with priorities.]

## References

[Primary docs, original papers, dataset/model terms.]

## Example Commands

[Preparation, training if applicable, evaluation and inference commands.]

## Expected Output

[Files, shapes, fields and example formatting. Separate expectations from results.]

## Maturity and validation

| Stage | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Development | Small working implementation with clear contracts |
| Testing | Meaningful properties, errors and integration |
| Evaluation | Held-out protocol and failure analysis |
| Optimization | Same workload before/after; correctness preserved |
| Deployment | Reproducible package and rollback procedure |
| Monitoring | Observable quality, performance and data health |
